chunks: Therefore, to whosoever Allah gives wealth he should use it in extending good behaviour to his kinsmen, in entertaining, in releasing prisoners and the afflicted; in giving to the poor and to debtors, and he should endure (the troubles arising out of) the fulfilment of rights (of others) and hardships in expectation of reward. Certainly, the achievement of these qualities is the height of greatness in this world and achievement of the distinctions of the next world; if Allah so wills.
ai.seo_question: What are the recommended ways to spend wealth according to Shia ethical teachings?
ai.summary: Attributed to Imam Ali in Nahj al-Balagha, this passage categorizes wealth as a divine trust (amanah) to be deployed for social welfare, reflecting the Shia emphasis on the moral obligation of the wealthy to alleviate societal burdens. It links material generosity with spiritual resilience, framing the endurance of hardships and fulfillment of rights as essential components of achieving both worldly dignity and eternal success.
